title: Contact span gave no clear count-adjusted link to repeated coherence in 35 inputs to one leech motor neuron
abstract: We tested whether the path span of contacts from one input relates to repeated complex coherence with a motor neuron. We used linked anatomy and voltage imaging from one leech ganglion. In 35 mapped input trees with at least two contacts, the count-adjusted partial rank correlation was -0.06949 for swimming and 0.18030 for left local bending. Whole-input label shuffles kept each exact contact count fixed. The Holm-adjusted two-sided p values were 0.59645 and 0.52780. Descriptive 97.5% input bootstrap intervals were -0.39793 to 0.27874 and -0.23274 to 0.57591. Mean pair distance and phase-only checks did not establish a new finding. The data give no clear evidence for this link, but the wide intervals do not show equivalence. One animal, selected inputs, possible tracing fragments, uncertain activity matches, and absent raw trace errors limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, random reference draws, independent checks, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Partial rank correlations for contact span and repeated complex coherence, with count-preserving label references. The data cover 35 inputs to one motor neuron in one leech. The draws are not samples of animals.
